prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Code · CLI flags (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Flag" · longest unbreakable word 106px · one-line width 204px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 114px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 477px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Document CLI flags so readers can choose an option and understand its type, default, and effect.","reading":"Readers will scan flag names first, then read across the row to compare the type, default, and description. Descriptions can use multiple lines; those taller rows can also accommodate wrapped flag aliases.","groups":["Flag identifies the option; Type and Default are compact attributes that belong together for comparison.","Description explains the effect of each flag and needs the most flexible width."],"keep_intact":["Individual flag names and placeholders, including --inspect-brk=[host]:port.","Type names and default values, especially 127.0.0.1:9229.","Individual words in descriptions."],"may_wrap":["Descriptions at word boundaries.","Multiple flag aliases within a cell, between the aliases."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[180,76,135,328],"idea":"Balance readable flag names with a generous description column, allowing aliases and descriptions to wrap where needed."},{"name":"B","widths":[127,76,135,381],"idea":"Give descriptions the most space while retaining enough width for each individual flag name."},{"name":"C","widths":[225,76,135,283],"idea":"Keep the full flag entries on one line to support rapid scanning, with descriptions taking more of the wrapping."}]}
